acceptanceGrade: REJECT on the artifact's own deliverable. Every prohibition is honoured — no OS, architecture or filesystem value appears anywhere, no Rosetta, no fixture byte. But the artifact exists to name an initial state and its one record contains none. This subject had the strongest available defence of the three input corpora I have now reviewed, because two of its class's coordinates are genuinely RESERVED; it still fails, for reasons set out below.
thirdConsecutiveOnThisDefectDisclosure: This is the third input corpus in a row I have rejected on the same defect, which is a pattern a coordinator should scrutinise rather than accept on my say-so. I re-derived it here: pins, four-way class equality, sibling-shape comparison, and above all the availability test were recomputed against G22's own source. G22's defence is materially stronger than G16's or G19's — the filesystem selector and the version/build selector are both RESERVED on this gate — so the question was live rather than settled by momentum, and I record exactly why the reserved coordinates do not make the emptiness forced.

shouldFix.title: An input corpus whose one initial state contains no initial state
shouldFix.finding: The purpose is to 'Continue leftover-design of OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING by naming the initial state of the one live G22 v1 corpus class', and whatIsAuthored claims 'One named initial state'. The record holds exactly four fields: an id that is a slug of the class name, memberVerbatim which is the class name, fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED, and assertsNamedNotAuthored which is a one-element list containing the class name again. There is no platform, no hostility kind, no live-cell member, no coordinate of any sort. Nothing in the artifact says what state a G22 harness would start in.
shouldFix.againstTheDocumentClass: Four sibling input corpora carry substantive per-state content — permission-fx5's four named revocation positions, permission-fx11's crashBetween with its behavioural flags, doctor-fc-ro's fourteen variantClass/degradedCase/consentClass/auditWrite records, permission-r6-r10's two race/outcome/whyDeterministic states. In each, the NOT-AUTHORED markers hang off a state that has been named.
shouldFix.addsNothingOverTheCatalogItConsumes: g22-named-corpus-catalog.v1, already accepted and pinned here, carries per class an id, memberVerbatim, slashJoinerVerbatim, exactByteIntentVerbatim, passPropertyVerbatim, fixtureBytes and filesystemSelectorPopulated — seven fields, including an explicit marker for the reserved axis. This artifact's four are a strict subset. It advances the leftover-design by nothing a later authoring cycle could not read from the catalog.
shouldFix.theStrongestDefenceAndWhyItFails: The defence here is real and I want it recorded, because it is stronger than at either sibling. Two of this class's coordinates genuinely cannot be named: G22 v1 records the filesystem token as this gate's TCB filesystem selector with standing RESERVED and matrixStanding INCOMPLETE until a later population packet, and records versionOrBuildSelector as RESERVED with notALiveHarnessCellMember true. Naming either would populate a reserved table, which the dispatch forbids. But that constrains two coordinates, not the state. The same source openly enumerates the four D-002 platforms — macos/arm64, macos/x86_64, linux/x86_64, linux/arm64 — in a top-level platforms key and in the class's own exactByteIntent, defines the hostile environment as presented undeclared or alternate libc/framework/cert/font/ICU/tool objects, alternate loaders, and ambient system-class substitutes on a clean machine, and names four live-cell members supplied by this very class: full loader trace, identity/version allowlist, negative undeclared resolution, and alternate-loader search. It further bounds any state by excluding Windows as a cell and excluding Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon as a macos/x86_64 cell. So a platform cell under the hostility family, with the filesystem coordinate marked RESERVED, is namable without populating anything. That is exactly the family's discipline — permission-fx5 names one coordinate and marks four NOT-AUTHORED — and G22 v1 models it itself by publishing platforms alongside filesystems.standing RESERVED.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing stated is false, no row moves, the artifact binds NOTHING, every prohibition is honoured, and OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING remains open on both the gate join and the DR-126 row join, which I verified.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Name at least one initial state per D-002 platform cell under the hostility family, carrying the four live-cell members, with the filesystem selector and version/build selector marked RESERVED rather than populated — the same shape the catalog already uses in filesystemSelectorPopulated.
shouldFix.notAssertedByThisFinding: I do not author any initial state, name a filesystem or version/build selector value, populate a per-OS table, invent Rosetta, or assert how many states the class should carry.

consideredAndDeclined.why: Declined after reading the source in full, and this was a genuinely open question rather than a formality. Two coordinates are RESERVED and cannot be named. But four D-002 platforms are openly enumerated in G22 v1's own platforms key and exactByteIntent, three hostility kinds are defined, four live-cell members are named, and Windows and Rosetta cells are expressly excluded. Marking the reserved coordinates while naming the available ones is precisely what the sibling corpora do and what G22 v1 itself models. The reservation constrains coordinates, not the existence of a state.

independence.otherReviewerHandling: No Codex verdict exists for this subject; I opened none and invented none. The Codex path is named and unwritten. I opened no Codex file in this review — none of the four cited artifacts has one.
independence.priorParticipation: All four Claude-lane verdicts this artifact pins are my lane's, and one is unmistakably mine from earlier today: the g22-leftover-join verdict at 62dfa58e. The dominant risk in this cycle is sequence rather than authorship — three consecutive rejections on one defect in one document class. I answered it by treating the availability test as the live question and running it against material specific to this gate: the RESERVED filesystem selector, the RESERVED version/build selector, the four published D-002 platforms, the hostile-environment definition, the four live-cell members, and the Windows and Rosetta exclusions. None of that existed in the two preceding reviews.
independence.whatWouldHaveChangedTheVerdict: If G22 v1 had held the platform axis reserved as well as the filesystem and version/build axes, or if the hostility family and live-cell members had not been enumerated, then no state could have been named without populating a reserved table and this would have been an ACCEPT. That is the finding's falsifier and it was tested, not assumed.
independence.residualRisk: A coordinator reviewing three consecutive rejections should apply the check I applied: is the missing content enumerated in a source the artifact already pins? It is in all three, and the enumerations are entirely different — mutation kinds and release selections at G16, state-classes and file-04 negative tests at G19, platforms and hostility kinds here.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Sixteen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject b5eb39e3 at 0444, 5007 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's own head equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-126 token OPEN; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce and the artifact contains exactly nine 64-hex strings, all of them those pins. Every prohibition is honoured and I tested by value rather than keyword: zero OS names, zero architecture names, zero filesystem names, zero ikconfig vectors, zero fixture paths, and no SATISFIED or QUALIFIED anywhere. Rosetta and the reserved-table terms appear only in refusals, and the refusal to close OBL-RESERVED-TABLES is accurate — platform-tcb-leftover-join.v5 carries it and OBL-G22-FX-AUTHORING at leftoverDesign true on DR-126, read at source. The single class is identical four ways and the two slash-joined groups are held whole. The finding is the deliverable. The artifact exists to name an initial state and its one record contains none: a slug of the class name, the class name, a NOT-AUTHORED marker, and the class name again. This is my third consecutive rejection of an input corpus on this defect, so the coordinator should know how the question was tested rather than assumed, especially because G22's defence is the strongest of the three. Two of this class's coordinates genuinely cannot be named — G22 v1 records the filesystem token as this gate's TCB selector with standing RESERVED and matrixStanding INCOMPLETE pending a later population packet, and records versionOrBuildSelector as RESERVED and not a live-cell member. Naming either would populate a reserved table. But that constrains two coordinates, not the state. The same source openly enumerates the four D-002 platforms in a top-level key and in the class's own exactByteIntent, defines hostile environment as presented undeclared or alternate libc, framework, cert, font, ICU and tool objects together with alternate loaders and ambient system-class substitutes on a clean machine, names four live-cell members supplied by this very class, and bounds any state by excluding Windows and excluding Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon as a macos/x86_64 cell. A platform cell under the hostility family with the filesystem coordinate marked RESERVED is namable without populating anything — which is exactly the discipline permission-fx5 uses in naming one coordinate and marking four NOT-AUTHORED, and which G22 v1 models itself by publishing platforms alongside a RESERVED filesystems standing. The catalog this corpus consumes carries seven fields per class including filesystemSelectorPopulated, an explicit marker for the reserved axis; the corpus's four are a strict subset. Had the platform axis been reserved too, or had the hostility family and live-cell members not been enumerated, no state could have been named without breaching the dispatch and this would have been an ACCEPT. That falsifier was tested. It is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because nothing stated is false and the obligation remains open on both joins. Declined and recorded: the 'this catalog' self-reference, which has a precedent I accepted at doctor-fc-ro-input-corpus.v3, and the absence of recordedInputs, which is the input-corpus form.
